newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian nuclear reactor restarted after problem.
newsitem.headline: Russian nuclear reactor restarted after problem.

text.p: Russian authorities restarted a nuclear reactor at a Siberian chemical plant on Sunday, one day after it was shut down because of a malfunction, Itar-Tass news agency said.

The reactor, in the city of Seversk about 3,000 km (1,875 miles) east of Moscow, was shut down after a drop in the cold water supply to its cooling system, forcing Seversk and nearby Tomsk to switch to emergency heating systems.

Tass quoted regional deputy governor Yusup Galyamov as saying there had been no radiation leak and that the reactor was expected to reach its normal capacity on Monday. Normal heating supplies were to be resumed as capacity increased, he said.

NTV commercial television said water had seeped into a faulty fuel rod at the reactor and reacted with uranium. It said a second reactor at the chemical plant was closed for routine maintenance earlier this month.
